description: The Toxics Release Inventory tracks how industrial and federal facilities in the United States manage listed toxic chemicals. Facilities that meet the reporting requirements submit data every year on releases to air, water and land, transfers off site, recycling, energy recovery, treatment and pollution prevention, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency publishes them with tools that add context. Coverage is national, per facility, with yearly data. Access is free through the TRI Toolbox: Basic data files as CSV grouped by year for each state or the whole country (last updated 12 November 2025, with forms processed to 5 November 2025), Basic Plus files of ten tab-delimited tables with every data element of the reporting form, an interactive national analysis, and the Risk-Screening Environmental Indicators (RSEI) model that compares potential impacts of releases. As a U.S. Government work the data are in the public domain. Caveats: reporting thresholds exclude small facilities and some sectors, quantities are facility estimates, and the latest year is preliminary until reprocessed. For simulation it gives the chemical inventories and release pathways of industrial plants for hazard exposure, natech and environmental impact scenarios, and emergency planning around chemical sites. Related catalogue records include the EPA Facility Registry Service, which links TRI facilities to other programmes, and the European Industrial Emissions Portal.
